newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: French fighter firms open UAE offset office.
newsitem.headline: French fighter firms open UAE offset office.

text.p: Three French fighter aircraft manufacturers opened an offset office in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday to help boost their chances of winning a multi-million-dollar defence contract.
The United Arab Emirates Offsets Group (UOG) said in a statement the new office was set up by Dassault Aviation, Snecma, and Thomson-CSF.

"The opening of this office reaffirms the three firms' commitment to set up and develop useful and profitable projects under the offset programme and with private sector participation," said the statement faxed to Reuters.

"These firms are manufacturing the Mirage-2000 jets owned by the UAE air force and manufacture the Rafale jets which is taking part in the competition to meet the special needs of the UAE's future air combat aircraft," it added.
The opening comes ahead of Abu Dhabi's IDEX arms show to be held March 16-19 when the UAE is expected to announce several arms deals.

The UAE, which has a defence pact and several large arms contracts with France, has been deliberating buying a mix of up to 30 Mirage 2000-5 and Rafale fighters from Dassault, industry sources have said.
Snecma and Thomson are among the main companies along with Dassault in building the Rafale systems.
The UAE, which already flies a fleet of 36 Mirage 2000's, wants multi-role, long-range aircraft with superior air-to-air combat capability, officials say.

The oil-rich United Arab Emirates, which has emerged as a key customer in the international arms market, launched the UOG in July 1990 when the UAE activated a plan to buy high-tech weapons worth billions of dollars.
Defence companies are required to invest in projects with local investors in 49/51 joint ventures that generate added value to the UAE over a period of seven years.
